title: Safety Zones
cross_references: Common Denominators of Fire Behavior on Tragedy Fires

nodes.text: Take advantage of heat barriers (lee side of ridges, large rocks, solid structures)

evidence.source_text: Take advantage of heat barriers such as lee side of ridges, large rocks, or solid structures.

nodes.text: Burn out safety zones prior to fire front arrival when possible

evidence.source_text: When possible, burn out safety zones prior to arrival of the fire front.

nodes.text: Avoid locations upslope, downwind, chimneys, saddles, narrow canyons, steep escape routes

evidence.source_text: Avoid locations that are upslope or downwind from the fire, chimneys, saddles, narrow canyons, and steep, uphill escape routes.

nodes.text: Ensure safety zones are not intended for structure protection
Calculate separation distance: at least four times the maximum continuous flame height

evidence.source_text: Separation distance between the firefighter and the flames should be at least four times the maximum continuous flame height.

nodes.text: Adjust calculations for wind and slope: larger separation distances required

evidence.source_text: Since calculations assume no wind and no slope, safety zones downwind or upslope from the fire will require larger separation distances.

nodes.text: Calculate area in acres for a 3-person engine crew

evidence.source_text: Area in acres is calculated to allow for distance separation on all sides for a 3-person engine crew (1 acre is approximately the size of a football field, or 208’ by 208’).
